assessment: This fundamental work substantially advances our understanding of cortical remapping in people with congenital or acquired missing hands. The evidence supporting the idea that remapping may not follow cortical proximity but instead functional rules as to how the effector is used are compelling, with rigorous univariate and multivariate analyses applied to functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging data. Importantly, the authors suggest this is mostly the case for one-handers but not for amputees for who the reorganization seems more limited in general.
